digest.top_line: PEACE-1 at 7.7y: abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (0.65-0.87) in de novo mCSPC; triplet vs ADT+docetaxel HR 0.68, 8y OS 40.3% vs 27.1%.
digest.tldr: Prostate carries the day: PEACE-1 long-term f/u supports abiraterone added to ADT+docetaxel in de novo mCSPC, while SOC+RT median OS 4.6y matched SOC, with no RT-attributable OS HR in source. Breast brings two single-arm HER2+ CNS phase IIs pairing RT with HER2-directed therapy: BRIDGET (SRS then tucatinib, 18-mo iPFS 59%) and INSPIRE-LM (RT then IT HP, mOS 36.2 mo).

sites.intro: Both HER2+ CNS studies are single-arm phase II with no RT-omitted arm, so RT's contribution can't be separated from the HER2-directed therapy.

studies.name: INSPIRE-LM
studies.tldr: mOS 36.2 mo (95% CI 19.4-NR), 12-mo OS 79% after RT then IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab in HER2+ breast LM; single-arm phase II, N=30.

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase II, N=30, conference abstract with open-ended CIs; concurrent systemic therapy allowed and no comparator, so neither RT nor IT contribution is isolated.
verdict.audience: HER2+ breast leptomeningeal metastasis, KPS ≥60, life expectancy >8 wk

studies.significance: Nearly every pt (97%) had WBRT or proton CSI before or at entry, so the survival figure describes a combined RT then IT sequence, not IT therapy alone. Dose, fractionation and the CSI vs WBRT split are not reported, which leaves open whether whole-neuraxis coverage is required before IT HER2 therapy.
studies.monday_clinic: In HER2+ breast LM with KPS ≥60 and expected survival beyond 8 weeks, this supports discussing RT followed by IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab, ideally on trial; it does not inform pts with poor PS or HER2-negative LM.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multi-institutional, **single-arm phase II**, N=30 enrolled Nov 2022 to May 2026. Median follow-up 26 months. Conference abstract (ESMO 2026, 1768RO).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **HER2+ breast LM**, life expectancy >8 weeks, **KPS ≥60**. Median age 48 (33-65); 15 pts (50%) had baseline KPS ≤70.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **IT trastuzumab 80 mg + IT pertuzumab 80 mg**, the previously reported RP2D. Systemic agents could continue if they controlled extra-CNS disease and LM had developed on them.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RT completed before IT therapy; **not required if prior intracranial RT**. **WBRT or proton CSI in 29 (97%)**, on study or before entry. Dose, fractionation and target split not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary objective: OS** after study treatment. Secondary: LM-PFS and LM response.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Most common G≥2 AEs attributed to IT therapy: nausea/vomiting 10%, fatigue 7%, headache 7%. No RT-attributable toxicity reported.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Authors describe this as **the longest median OS reported to date in HER2+ LM**. No contemporaneous comparator in the trial, so that claim rests on cross-trial comparison with differently selected cohorts.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HER2+ breast LM pts with KPS ≥60 and >8 wk life expectancy, nearly all of whom received cranial or craniospinal RT. Does not represent HER2-negative LM, poor-PS pts, or an IT-therapy-without-RT approach.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Eligibility (life expectancy >8 wk, KPS ≥60) selects for better-prognosis LM. **Concurrent systemic therapy** confounds attribution, and the prior-lines figure (median 34, range 1-9) is internally inconsistent.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: A durable OS and LM-PFS signal with low G≥2 IT toxicity supports a randomized test. It does not settle whether RT, IT HER2 blockade, or modern systemic therapy drives the outcome, or whether CSI adds over WBRT.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 97% received WBRT or proton CSI ahead of IT therapy, so the outcome reflects an RT-first sequence. Dose, fractionation and the CSI vs WBRT split are unreported, so the trial cannot yet guide target-volume choice before IT HER2 therapy.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: IT trastuzumab 80 mg + pertuzumab 80 mg gave CR 17% and PR 17% with G≥2 nausea/vomiting only 10%. Systemic therapy continued alongside, so IT dual HER2 blockade is an add-on to, not a replacement for, systemic control.

open_questions: Contribution of RT vs IT HER2 therapy to survival
Proton CSI vs WBRT before IT therapy
Randomized confirmation of IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab in HER2+ LM

studies.name: BRIDGET
studies.tldr: Median iPFS not reached vs 5.0 mo historical control (p<0.0001); 18-mo iPFS 59% adding tucatinib to HP/T-DM1 after SRS for isolated intracranial progression.
details: 🔍 Single-arm phase II, N=48 enrolled, 47 evaluable; NCT05323955

subdetails: HER2+ MBC, first or second isolated intracranial event
Stable or no extracranial disease on HP or T-DM1
SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm, within 12 wks of enrollment
WBRT exclusionary; no prior HER2/EGFR TKI; ECOG PS 0-2

details: 💊 Tucatinib 300 mg BID added continuously to ongoing HP or T-DM1
🔍 Population: median age 53.5 yrs, 66% ER+, 66% no ECD, 93.6% HP backbone, 80.9% after first intracranial event

details.text: 📊 iPFS (RANO-BM) by timepoint, median f/u 19.6 mo (95% CI 15.6-26.1)

details: 📊 Intracranial progression in 17 pts (36.2%); median iPFS NR
📐 One-sample log-rank p<0.0001 vs H0 median iPFS 5 mo (one-sided α=0.05, 90% power)
📊 Extracranial progression rare: 2 pts (4.3%)
⚠️ Historical exponential control, not a concurrent SRS-alone arm; benefit size vs SRS + unchanged therapy unknown
⚠️ 12-to-18-mo iPFS drop 64% to 59%, yet 36.2% still progressed intracranially; no breakdown of local vs distant brain failure in source
🔗 Builds on HER2CLIMB intracranial activity (tucatinib + capecitabine/trastuzumab); here tucatinib without capecitabine

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase II against a historical 5.0-mo control; no randomised SRS-plus-continued-therapy comparator. Abstract-only, rapid oral.
verdict.audience: HER2+ MBC, isolated intracranial progression post-SRS, stable/no ECD on HP or T-DM1

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is distant brain control after SRS-only management: with WBRT excluded, iPFS held at 64% at 12 mo and 59% at 18 mo after adding tucatinib. That frames tucatinib as a partner to SRS rather than an argument for WBRT. Local vs distant intracranial failure is not split in the source.
studies.monday_clinic: In HER2+ MBC with a first isolated brain progression treated with SRS and stable or no extracranial disease on HP, this supports considering tucatinib added to ongoing therapy; it does not extend to pts with prior HER2 TKI exposure or WBRT.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Single-arm phase II**, N=48 enrolled, 47 evaluable. **Primary:** iPFS per RANO-BM vs a **historical exponential control (median 5.0 mo)**, one-sample log-rank, one-sided α=0.05, 90% power, N=43 evaluable planned.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **HER2+ MBC with a first or second isolated intracranial event** and stable/no extracranial disease on HP or T-DM1; ECOG PS 0-2; **no prior HER2/EGFR TKI**. Median age 53.5 yrs, 66% ER+, 66% no ECD, 80.9% enrolled after first event.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Tucatinib 300 mg BID** added continuously to ongoing HP (93.6%) or T-DM1.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm** within 12 wks before enrollment. **WBRT was exclusionary.** Dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: At median f/u 19.6 mo, intracranial progression in 17 pts (36.2%); **median iPFS not reached** (p<0.0001 vs H0 of 5 mo). iPFS **91% / 64% / 59%** at 6 / 12 / 18 mo. Extracranial progression 2 pts (4.3%).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **G≥3 AEs 15% (7/47).** Organ-specific AE breakdown not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: HER2CLIMB established tucatinib intracranial activity with capecitabine/trastuzumab; BRIDGET tests it **without capecitabine**, layered onto HP or T-DM1 after SRS. Current guidelines continue the same systemic regimen after local therapy, which is the practice this trial challenges.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HER2+ MBC pts with isolated intracranial progression after SRS, TKI-naive, on HP or T-DM1 with stable or no extracranial disease. Does not represent pts needing WBRT, with progressing extracranial disease, or with prior HER2/EGFR TKI.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The 5.0-mo historical control likely reflects older series and may understate modern SRS-alone iPFS. **Local vs distant brain failure is not separated**, and T-DM1 backbone n is small.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Intracranial control looks durable with a modest G≥3 rate, and extracranial progression was rare in this selected population. What is unsettled is how much iPFS SRS plus unchanged HP would achieve in the same pts, which only a randomised comparison answers.

studies.interpretation:
BRIDGET asks a question guidelines currently answer by default: after SRS for an isolated brain event in HER2+ MBC, keep the systemic regimen unchanged. The rationale for changing it comes from HER2CLIMB, where tucatinib showed intracranial activity, but that activity was measured with capecitabine and trastuzumab, in a broader brain-metastatic population. BRIDGET isolates a narrower scenario, the pt whose extracranial disease is controlled and whose brain is the only site of failure, and adds tucatinib to whatever HER2 backbone is working, almost always HP here. That is a cleaner clinical question than HER2CLIMB posed, and a more common one in practice.

The headline statistic needs careful reading. Beating a historical median of 5.0 mo with p<0.0001 sounds decisive, but the comparison is only as good as the control. A 5-month iPFS benchmark plausibly reflects older cohorts, some with WBRT-era or less selected populations, and may be pessimistic for modern pts who receive SRS to every lesion ≥5mm and stay on effective HP. The trial also enrolled a favorable group: 66% had no extracranial disease and 80.9% were at their first intracranial event. Some of the 91%, 64% and 59% iPFS at 6, 12 and 18 mo is therefore patient selection and SRS, not tucatinib. The size of the drug's contribution is not estimable from a single arm.

For the radiation oncologist, the more informative missing piece is the pattern of failure. 17 pts (36.2%) progressed intracranially, but the abstract does not separate treated-lesion recurrence from new metastases. Tucatinib's plausible value is suppressing distant brain failure, the event that drives repeat SRS or eventual WBRT. If most failures were new lesions, the drug did less than hoped; if most were local, SRS technique matters more than the systemic change. That split determines whether this strategy changes surveillance intervals and the threshold for repeat SRS.

Safety reads as manageable, with G≥3 AEs in 15%, and the regimen avoids capecitabine toxicity, which makes it practical for pts already tolerating HP long term. The T-DM1 backbone is too sparsely represented to support a conclusion for that group, and pts with prior TKI exposure were excluded, a population growing as tucatinib moves earlier.

What would make this wrong: a randomised comparison showing SRS plus unchanged HP achieves similar 12-to-18-month iPFS in an equally selected group. Until that exists, BRIDGET is a reasonable basis for discussing tucatinib after SRS in TKI-naive pts, not evidence that continuing the prior regimen alone is inferior.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: With WBRT excluded and SRS to all lesions ≥5mm, iPFS reached 59% at 18 mo after adding tucatinib, supporting SRS-alone strategies paired with a CNS-active TKI. Pattern of intracranial failure (in-field vs new lesions) is not reported in source.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Guidelines keep the same systemic regimen after local therapy for isolated CNS progression; this adds tucatinib 300 mg BID to HP or T-DM1 without switching backbone, with G≥3 AEs 15%. 93.6% were on HP, so T-DM1 data are thin.

open_questions: Benefit vs SRS plus unchanged HP in a randomised comparison
Local vs distant intracranial failure pattern with tucatinib
Activity after prior HER2 TKI exposure

studies.name: PEACE-1
studies.tldr: 7.7y f/u: abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (0.65-0.87) in de novo mCSPC; triplet vs ADT+docetaxel HR 0.68, 8y OS 40.3% vs 27.1%.
details: 🔍 Randomized phase III 2x2 factorial, 1:1:1:1, N=1173 de novo mCSPC (57% high-, 43% low-volume)
💊 SOC = ADT ± docetaxel; randomized additions: abiraterone/prednisone and/or prostate RT
📊 Abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.87), p=0.0001 at median f/u 7.7y
📊 Pooled median OS 6.1y with abiraterone vs 4.6y without; 8y OS 40.3% vs 29.5%

details.text: 📊 Median OS by randomized arm (y, 95% CI)
📊 ADT+docetaxel SOC subgroup (n=710): doublet vs triplet

details: 📐 No interaction with metastatic extent, p=0.56
⚠️ Low-volume triplet HR CI crosses 1 (0.52-1.05); OncoDaily reports p=0.091
⚠️ Docetaxel was SOC choice, not a randomized factor; doublet vs triplet is a subgroup of the abiraterone randomization
⚠️ Source discordance: high-volume 8y OS 20% vs 38% (abstract) vs 7y 22.4% vs 40.9% (OncoDaily); low-volume CI lower bound 0.52 vs 0.51
⚠️ RT arm: SOC+RT median OS 4.6y, same as SOC; no RT-attributable OS HR or volume split in source
⚠️ Abstract-level data only: no safety, subsequent-therapy or rPFS update in source

verdict.rationale: Long-term update of a randomized phase III; OS benefit persists and strengthens vs the 4.4y analysis. Triplet read rests on non-randomized docetaxel use; low-volume CI crosses 1.
verdict.audience: De novo mCSPC, high- or low-volume, on ADT ± docetaxel

studies.significance: The four-arm medians are the RT read: SOC+RT 4.6y matched SOC 4.6y, and SOC+RT+abiraterone reached 6.4y vs 5.7y for SOC+abiraterone, but no RT-attributable OS HR or volume split is reported in source. The prostate-RT decision in low-volume de novo disease still rests on earlier PEACE-1 reports, not this update.
studies.monday_clinic: In de novo mCSPC starting ADT plus docetaxel, high-volume especially, this supports adding abiraterone for OS; it does not address metachronous mCSPC, and the low-volume triplet estimate remains imprecise.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomized phase III, 2x2 factorial**, 1:1:1:1, N=1173. Long-term analysis at **median f/u 7.7y**; initial analysis was at 4.4y.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **De novo mCSPC**; 57% high-volume, 43% low-volume. SOC was ADT with or without docetaxel; 710 pts received **ADT+docetaxel**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Randomized additions to SOC: **abiraterone acetate plus prednisone** and/or **prostate RT**. Docetaxel was part of SOC, not a randomized factor.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Prostate RT was one factorial arm. Median OS **4.6y SOC+RT vs 4.6y SOC**; dose, fractionation and an RT-attributable OS HR are not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Abiraterone OS **HR 0.75 (0.65-0.87), p=0.0001**, tightened from **HR 0.82 (0.69-0.98)** at 4.4y. Triplet vs doublet **HR 0.68 (0.56-0.82)**, consistent across volume (interaction p=0.56).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Extends the 2022 Lancet PEACE-1 OS result with more mature follow-up. Sits alongside ARASENS as triplet evidence on a docetaxel backbone, here with abiraterone and a far longer follow-up.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents de novo mCSPC on ADT ± docetaxel, high- or low-volume. Does not represent metachronous mCSPC after prior local therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Reports disagree on high-volume landmark OS (8y 20% vs 38% abstract, 7y 22.4% vs 40.9% OncoDaily). No safety, rPFS or post-progression therapy data in source to contextualize the late OS gain.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The abiraterone HR improved with maturity rather than eroding, which argues against an early-separation artifact. The **low-volume triplet** question and the **RT arm's OS contribution** are not settled by this update.

studies.interpretation:
The most informative feature of this update is the direction the hazard ratio moved. At 4.4 years abiraterone gave an OS HR of 0.82 with an upper bound of 0.98, a result that was positive but close enough to the line that a skeptic could argue it would fade as control-arm patients reached life-prolonging therapy at progression. At 7.7 years the estimate is 0.75 (0.65-0.87). Benefits that come from delaying progression and are then neutralized by effective salvage usually converge with time; this one widened. That pattern is more consistent with a durable biological effect of earlier androgen-axis intensification than with a transient lead. The caveat is that the source gives no data on post-progression therapy, so how much of the control arm eventually received an ARSI cannot be judged here.

The triplet result is where most readers will focus, and it deserves a careful read of what was randomized. Docetaxel was part of standard of care at the treating team's discretion, so the 710-patient docetaxel cohort is a subgroup defined by a post-randomization-independent but non-randomized choice. Within that cohort, abiraterone versus no abiraterone remains a randomized comparison, so the HR of 0.68 (0.56-0.82) is a fair estimate of adding abiraterone to ADT plus docetaxel. What it does not answer is whether triplet therapy beats an ARSI doublet without docetaxel, which is the question most clinicians are actually weighing. ARASENS addressed the triplet question with darolutamide, and PEACE-1 now reinforces it with a different agent and longer follow-up; neither trial randomized docetaxel against no docetaxel on an ARSI backbone.

Volume is the second axis. The interaction p of 0.56 says the data cannot distinguish the high- and low-volume effects, and the low-volume HR of 0.74 is numerically similar to the high-volume 0.68. But the low-volume interval runs to 1.05, and low-volume patients are the group in whom docetaxel itself is least favored. Reading a non-significant interaction test as proof of equal benefit in an underpowered subgroup is a common error; the more defensible statement is that low-volume patients who were given docetaxel do not appear to be harmed by adding abiraterone, and the point estimate leans toward benefit.

For a radiation oncologist the update is thinner. The four-arm medians show SOC+RT at 4.6 years, identical to SOC, and SOC+RT+abiraterone at 6.4 versus 5.7 years for SOC+abiraterone. No RT-attributable OS hazard ratio and no volume-stratified RT analysis are reported in the source, and those are what would move a decision about prostate RT in low-volume de novo disease. The four-arm medians should not be read as an RT effect in either direction without them.

Finally, the abstract and the OncoDaily write-up disagree on the high-volume landmark (8-year 20% vs 38% in the abstract, 7-year 22.4% vs 40.9% in the press piece) and slightly on the low-volume interval. The hazard ratios agree closely, so the direction is not in question, but landmark survival figures should be taken from the full publication before being quoted to patients or colleagues.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SOC+RT median OS 4.6y matched SOC 4.6y, and SOC+RT+abiraterone 6.4y vs SOC+abiraterone 5.7y, with no RT-attributable OS HR or low-volume RT split in source. This update does not resolve the prostate-RT question in low-volume de novo mCSPC.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Triplet vs ADT+docetaxel holds at 7.7y: HR 0.68 (0.56-0.82), 8y OS 40.3% vs 27.1%, interaction by volume p=0.56. High-volume pts carry the clearest gain (HR 0.68, 0.54-0.85); the low-volume CI crosses 1, so the docetaxel-backbone decision there stays less settled.

open_questions: Does triplet beat an ARSI doublet without docetaxel?
Long-term OS effect of prostate RT by metastatic volume?
Is low-volume triplet benefit real given CI crossing 1?

papers.title: Long-term overall survival with abiraterone acetate plus prednisone in the PEACE-1 phase 3 trial for de novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2215O · Proffered paper: Genitourinary tumours, prostate, penile and testis · 2026-10-24 · presented by Karim Fizazi (Lille, France) · NCT01957436

Background: Recent trials demonstrated the benefit of systemic treatment intensification in mCSPC. However, long-term analyses are rare, especially for pharma industry trials. PEACE-1 (NCT01957436) is a 2x2 factorial phase 3 randomized trial that tested the addition of abiraterone acetate/prednisone (abiraterone) and/or prostate radiotherapy (RT) to standard of care (SOC) consisting of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with or without docetaxel.
Methods: 1173 men (57% high-, 43% low-volume) with de novo mCSPC were randomized (1:1:1:1) to SOC, SOC+abiraterone, SOC+RT or SOC+abiraterone+RT. The initial analysis (median follow-up: 4.4 years [y]) showed abiraterone improved overall survival (OS) (HR: 0·82, 95% CI 0·69–0·98; p=0·030) (Fizazi K, Lancet 2022). Here we report long-term follow-up results.
Results: The median follow-up is 7.7 y. Abiraterone significantly improved survival (HR: 0.75 [95%CI: 0.65-0.87], p=0.0001) with median OS of 4.6 y (4.1-5.5) for SOC, 4.6 y (4.0-5.2) for SOC+RT, 5.7 y (4.8-6.6) for SOC+abiraterone, and 6.4 y (5.5-7.6) for SOC+RT+abiraterone, respectively. In the subgroup of 710 patients who received ADT+docetaxel as their SOC, adding abiraterone also improved survival (HR: 0.68 [0.56-0.82]), with a median OS of 4.4 y (4.0-4.9) for ADT+docetaxel (doublet) and 6.2 y (5.2-7.3) for ADT+docetaxel+abiraterone (triplet), resulting in 8-year survival rates of 27.1% (22.1-32.9) and 40.3% (34.3-46.6), respectively. The favorable effect of triplet therapy on OS was independent of metastatic extent (interaction test p= 0.56): median OS was 3.5 y (3.2-4.0) vs 4.6y (3.9-6.1) in patients with high-volume (HR: 0.68 [0,54; 0,85]) and 6.2 y (5.4-8.1) vs 7.8 y (6.4-NR) in patients with low-volume (HR: 0.74 [0.52-1.05]), for doublet versus triplet respectively. In patients with high-volume, 8-year OS rates were 20% (14.6-26.7) with doublet vs 38% (31.3-45.1) with triplet therapy.
Conclusions: Very long-term follow-up shows a major OS benefit of adding abiraterone to SOC for patients with mCSPC, irrespective of metastatic extent. Triplet therapy with ADT+docetaxel+abiraterone is associated with almost twice as many long-term survivors in some subgroups.
Clinical trial identification: NCT01957436.

papers.title: Radiation therapy followed by intrathecal (IT) trastuzumab/pertuzumab in the management of HER2+ breast leptomeningeal metastasis: Results from a phase II multi-institutional study, (INSPIRE-LM)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1768RO · Rapid oral 2: Breast cancer, advanced stage · 2026-10-26 · presented by Kamran Ahmed (Tampa, United States of America) · NCT04588545

Background: Treatment options for HER2+ leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) remain limited. We previously reported 80 mg as the recommended phase II dose of IT pertuzumab alongside 80 mg IT trastuzumab and now report preliminary results from the phase II study.
Methods: The study is a multi-institutional, phase II trial of radiation therapy (RT) followed by IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab in the management of HER2+ breast LM. HER2+ LM patients with a life expectancy > 8 weeks, and KPS ≥ 60 were eligible. RT was completed prior to the delivery of IT therapy but was not required in patients that received prior intracranial RT. Patients could continue treatment with systemic agents if controlling disease and LM developed while on these therapies. The primary objective was to evaluate overall survival (OS) following study treatment. Secondary objectives included LM progression free survival (LM-PFS) and LM response.
Results: A total of 30 patients were enrolled between November 2022 and May 2026. Median age was 48 (range: 33-65) and 15 patients (50%) had a baseline KPS </= 70. The median number of prior systemic therapies was 34 (range: 1-9). Most patients received whole brain radiation therapy or proton cranial spinal irradiation (n=29; 97%) either prior to IT therapy or before study entry. Median follow-up is 26 months. The study met its predetermined endpoint for OS. Median survival is 36.2 months (95% CI: 19.4 – Not reached (NR)) with a 12-month OS of 79%. Median LM progression free survival (LM-PFS) is 19.3 months (95% CI 7.2 – NR) with a 12-month LM-PFS of 61%. The best LM response was a complete response in 5 (17%), partial response in 5 (17%), and stable disease in 17 (57%). The most common grade ≥ 2 adverse events attributed to IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab included nausea/vomiting (n=3; 10%), fatigue (n=2; 7%), and headache (n=2; 7%). Currently, twelve patients (40%) continue study therapy with 38.7 months as the longest treatment duration.
Conclusions: The study met its predetermined endpoint for OS with the longest median OS reported to date in HER2+ LM. Complete responses were noted in a subset of patients. IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab should be considered in the management of HER2+ LM.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04588545.

papers.title: BRIDGET: A phase II trial of tucatinib added to trastuzumab/pertuzumab or ado-trastuzumab emtansine after isolated intracranial progression in patients with advanced HER2-positive breast cancer
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1767RO · Rapid oral 2: Breast cancer, advanced stage · 2026-10-26 · presented by Sarah Sammons (Baltimore, United States of America) · NCT05323955

Background: Isolated CNS relapse/progression (ICP) is a frequent occurrence in patients (pts) with HER2+ MBC. Current guidelines recommend local therapy and continuation of same systemic regimen. The impact of adjusting the systemic regimen to include a CNS-active agent is unknown. Tucatinib demonstrated significant intracranial activity in HER2CLIMB when delivered with capecitabine/trastuzumab. BRIDGET is a prospective trial to add a brain-penetrant TKI post radiation to ongoing therapy in attempts to prolong intracranial disease control in pts with stable or no extracranial disease (ECD).
Methods: Single-arm phase II trial of pts with HER2+ MBC experiencing a first or second isolated intracranial event with stable/no ECD on HP or T-DM1 within 12 wks of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). Key eligibility: ECOG PS 0–2; SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm, no prior HER2/EGFR TKI. Whole-brain radiation was exclusionary. Tucatinib 300 mg BID was added continuously to ongoing HP or T-DM1 therapy. Primary endpoint: intracranial PFS (iPFS) per RANO-BM compared with a historical exponential control (median of 5.0 mos) using a one-sample log-rank test (one-sided α=0.05; 90% power; N=43 evaluable).
Results: Of 48 enrolled pts, 47 were evaluable (median age 53.5 yrs; 66% ER+). Most pts (66%) had no ECD at enrollment, were treated with backbone HP (93.6%) and enrolled after their first intracranial event (80.9%). At a median follow-up of 19.6 mos (95% CI 15.6–26.1), intracranial progression occurred in 17 pts (36.2%); median iPFS was not reached (one-sample log-rank p<0.0001 for H0: median iPFS=5 mos). The 6-, 12-, and 18-mo iPFS rates were 91%, 64%, and 59%, respectively. Extracranial progression was rare (2 pts, 4.3%). The safety profile was favorable: grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 15% (7/47).
Conclusions: The addition of tucatinib to HP after radiation met the study’s primary endpoint, with more than half of patients remaining free of intracranial progression at 18 months. These findings support the addition of early tucatinib after local therapy as a well-tolerated strategy to improve intracranial disease control in a HER2+ isolated brain progression population.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05323955.
